analysis:
I found no concrete regression in the supplied source, but the segment-retention change needs a follow-up check outside it.

1) EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift (head lines 24-42, 50-62): The paged KV pool now keeps up to min(2 GiB, grant/8) of free segments across requests. It is on by default and can be turned off with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0. Segments are zeroed on the host by default. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS=0 switches back to device fills. This changes the residual-data posture relevant to T-028 and A-001, because release-time retirement with device zero fill and a stream fence is replaced by reuse of previously evaluated segments.
   - I could not see PagedKVBackend or PagedKVPoolConfig. They do not show whether a retained segment is scrubbed, or fully overwritten or masked, before it is handed to a different request or consumer.
   - They also do not show whether the zeroing runs on the reuse path and is ordered correctly against GPU work.
   - The segments stay inside the same provider process and the same attested boundary. Co-tenant residue is already an accepted T-028 concern, so I am not raising this as a finding, but it should be checked.
   - The environment keys are operator-controlled. That is within the ADV-001 trust model and is not a new boundary.
   - The retained bytes are bounded by the admitted grant. I saw no accounting bypass.

2) MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation.swift (head lines 82-86, 113-116, 140-143, 168-171, 178-187) and MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift (patch lines ~963 and ~1074): An .insufficientCapacity refusal now computes a shortfall through ledger.capacityShortfall and calls an optional onRefusal, wired to budget.directChargeRefusalSignal(). The thrown errors are unchanged (reservationRejected), and .stalePolicy behavior is unchanged. Signal calls in validate and the adopt/reserve paths run under the reservation's NSLock. Open questions for integration:
   - directChargeRefusalSignal is not in the supplied evidence. It must stay non-blocking and must not re-enter the reservation or ledger locks.
   - A consumer who can send media that is repeatedly refused could trigger reclaim work, such as cache eviction or slot shrinking. Whether that is rate-limited or only coalesced is not visible.
   - signalShortfall(growthBytes: 0) in validate is a heuristic, but it only sizes the deficit.

The reservation refusal and ownership semantics are otherwise preserved. No change was seen to the A-001 sealing, attestation or authorization flows.
